channel.title: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight" - Psychic portals allow Foundation to contact dead souls in Hell

item.title: Re: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for reviewing my concept. I was aware that a few SCPs dealt with Christian-like concepts of Hell, though I had not seen SCP-4661 or Arcadia.

My plan was to use a detached, clinical tone in Containment Procedures and Description, and then to use a slightly more narrative, direct style in a string of Exploration Logs, Interviews, and Incident Reports.

The SCP would include descriptions of how MTFs dealt with manifesting demons (I was being facetious with the "badass demon-killing"), as well as researchers' notes on these entities. But the main focus would be on the people exploring "Hell" (the Foundation would refer to it as the Abyss.)

Over several interview logs, the Mediums who access the SCP would try to explain what they see. The Mediums, who are of several faiths: Christian, Jewish, Islamic, Hindu, Buddhist; would experience the Abyss in different ways, since it is a metaphysical reality, and the human mind often needs to visualize and familiarize abstract concepts. What the Mediums see is often dark and traumatic, and repeated visits to the Abyss often eat away at their mental health.

Interviewing researchers do find a common theme among the Mediums' varying accounts: the horror of the Abyss is self-imposed. More than a simple torture chamber, the souls and entities within are locked in personal reveries, tortured by their own insanity, loneliness, and self-hatred as they constantly relive horrific fantasies and tear each other apart.

I agree that disturbing visuals alone can't carry an article. The central horror in this article is conceptual; existential. The visuals serve to fully realize that; to turn the scary idea into a tangible nightmare.

I had intended for the SCP itself: the Portals, Virgil Events, and such, to be rather mysterious. Mediums always experience some kind of Lobby or Antechamber. This room is manned by a figure in a white mask, (dubbed SCP-XXXX-A) who guides the visitor to the soul they ask for, and/or lets them explore Hell, but never explains itself. I would be happy to go more into this part of the SCP if you think that would improve the article.

As for the Chaos Insurgency, I only mention it once. A dead spy who had information the Foundation needed was a good motive for it to start using this SCP. Is there a problem in using the Insurgency?

P.S.: Is MTF Psi-8 "Silencers" the right group for this SCP?

item.title: Re: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
This article boasts detailed and intense explorations of Hell; it depicts the mental breakdown of those who visit Hell; and it indulges in the occasional badass demon-killing action scene (described via interview logs, as appropriate to an SCP article).

So everything here seems like a rather dry rendition of the Protestant imagining of Hell, and if I'm understanding you right then the harrowing details of the experience and demon-killing are essentially the selling points of all this. And I'm not totally convinced that's a viable model — disturbing visuals are fine as complements but they usually can't make a piece stand on its own.

Frankly I'm more interested in a fresh take on the Protestant Hell, or examining why the particular locations allow for travel to it, or why this infrastructure to visit Hell even exists. Lots of ways to play around with the set-pieces that I don't think are being taken advantage of here.

Additionally, are you planning to follow any central characters or discuss a particular conflict? I'm only getting the sense that there's this foray regarding the Chaos Insurgency (which hasn't… aged particularly well, if you don't feel familiar with site standards I recommend you read some newer articles) and then an incident where the Foundation realizes that doors work both ways.

If you're unfamiliar, by the way, Hell and demons have already been used somewhat on the site, particularly in the mini-canon of stories surrounding SCP-4661 and with the GOI Arcadia. I'd recommend reading through some of those stories to see what's been done and where you can expand the idea.

item.title: New Writer Seeking Greenlight: The ANTECHAMBER
item.content:encoded:
Potential SCP: Several locations around the globe that let psychics access a metaphysical gateway to Hell; allows them to communicate with the dead

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror (existential, graphic)

Page Layout:
Standard Order: Class; Containment; Description; Discovery; Exploration Logs and Addenda

Elevator Pitch: Several locations around the globe allow psychic individuals to access a metaphysical gateway to Hell. This allows them, and by proxy, the Foundation, to communicate with the dead. This SCP is useful, but dangerous: sometimes, something from the other side hitches a ride back to our world…

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

Certain locations will periodically undergo Virgil Events. During these events, magically skilled or psionically gifted individuals can access a kind of metaphysical lobby, hosted by a mysterious masked attendant. This Antechamber allows access to a vast, spiritual realm full of dead souls and entities, all in perpetual, self-inflicted agony. Mediums can find and speak to deceased individuals, and gain otherwise unobtainable information for the Foundation.

For example, the Foundation uses this SCP to contact a Chaos Insurgent spy who had been killed while trying to sabotage the Foundation; they able to wring out of the confused spirit the name of his accomplice, still hidden in Foundation ranks.

The Foundation sends many Mediums to explore and document the SCP. But over time, this eats away at their sanity. Moreover, there are occasional Geryon Events, where something will follow the Mediums back into the physical realm, and Foundation soldiers have to deal with them.

The SCP is called the Antechamber because the SCP actually refers to the Lobby-like chamber that Mediums experience when they access the SCP, which allows access to all of Hell.

Hook: This article boasts detailed and intense explorations of Hell; it depicts the mental breakdown of those who visit Hell; and it indulges in the occasional badass demon-killing action scene (described via interview logs, as appropriate to an SCP article).

Additional Notes: The ritual that allows access to this SCP was discovered in a book confiscated from a Marshall, Carter, & Dark shipment.
